brief: Wolfe raises its power-sector sentiment meter two notches to a 4. A broader AI sell-off hit the week, but CEG's second big deal, a 3.6 GW generation agreement with GOOGL (2.7 GW existing plus 890 MW uprates), followed CEG's 690 MW AMZN deal at Calvert Cliffs and TLN's news that Mac is retiring, Terry becomes CEO, and TLN will run a $1.5B accelerated buyback, and together these shifted sentiment back toward the IPPs. CEG stays atop Wolfe's IPP pecking order, followed by VST. Wolfe now estimates CEG is about 35% contracted on an EPS basis at full ramp, moving it ahead of TLN (previously the leader at low-30s% of free cash flow) and VST (low-20s% of EBITDA); NRG remains largely uncontracted pending its first data-center deal. On regulation, FERC accepted most of PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement proposal but sent back cost-allocation methodology for revision, pushing RBP's central procurement into early 2027, and separately rejected PJM's IRAS proposal except for the large-load registry. In Q3 commodities, PJM spot and forward power prices rose on record peak load and tight grid conditions, while ERCOT prices fell despite its own record peak load because renewables and storage absorbed the demand; natural gas and coal prices eased.
